name: French Bay, Titirangi
access: Otitori Bay Rd, Titirangi. 2 min from Titirangi village, small car park at the beach.
best: Bush amphitheatre opening onto the Manukau, moored boats, Titirangi village lights behind. Best west-side cinematic site.
hazards: Boats and swimmers in summer, mud at low tide, dense bush behind you eats video, narrow road parking.
note: No permit needed. Log the flight on AirShare. Dawn is glassy; the afternoon sea breeze comes straight up the bay.

name: Titirangi Beach
access: Titirangi Beach Rd, end of the road. Wharf + beach.
best: Wharf, boats and bush-fringed beach with the Manukau beyond. Good proximity flying around the wharf at low tide.
hazards: Busy little beach in summer, swimmers off the wharf, moored boats, tide
note: No permit. The wharf is the interesting line; keep clear of anyone fishing or swimming.

name: Laingholm Beach
access: Laingholm Beach via Victory Rd, Laingholm. Quiet residential no-exit road.
best: The quietest inlet on the Manukau side - bush, boats, big water views, almost nobody midweek.
hazards: Mudflats at low tide, narrow road with no formal parking, few people around if you need a hand retrieving.
note: Best seclusion score in west Auckland. Small local reserve, no permit required.

name: Blockhouse Bay Reserve
access: Blockhouse Bay Rd, car park at the reserve. 20 min from CBD.
best: Clifftop, bush, beach, wharf and full city skyline across the Manukau - the most varied flying in the west.
hazards: Popular with walkers and dog owners, swimmers at the beach, cliff edges, tide
note: No permit. Busiest of the west spots - go early or on a weekday.

name: Green Bay / Tauihu Beach
access: Green Bay Rd, beach reserve next to the shops.
best: Small sheltered beach with a bush backdrop and easy parking - a quick after-work spot.
hazards: Shops and traffic close by, swimmers, mud at low tide
note: No permit. Short session spot rather than a destination. Pin is the beach reserve at the end of the bay.

name: Parrs Park, Oratia
access: Parrs Park Drive off West Coast Rd, Oratia. 20 min from CBD.
best: Big open park with streams, mature trees and sports fields - room to tune, test and fly line-of-sight comfortably.
hazards: Sports fields in use, dog walkers, streams (no retrieval)
note: No permit. The best open-space test field in the west that is still outside the Whenuapai CTR.

name: Olympic Park, New Lynn
access: Portage Rd / Titirangi Rd, New Lynn. Car park off Portage Rd.
best: Flat sports park, good for tuning, GPS checks and race gates. Not scenic.
hazards: Sports fields in use most evenings and weekends, athletics crowds
note: No permit. Utility field only - don't make a trip for the scenery.

name: Awhitu Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Matakawau Point, Awhitu Peninsula. ~1 h 35 from CBD via Waiuku - a day trip, not an afternoon.
best: Wild west coast: black sand, cliffs, farmland, nobody. The best actual flying in this list if you'll do the paperwork.
hazards: Exposed coast, strong onshore wind, farm stock, permit conditions, long drive
note: Not on the banned regional-park list, so a drone permit is available through council. Apply before you go.

name: Woodhill Forest
access: Restall Rd or Woodhill Forest access off SH16, ~45 min from CBD.
best: Dunes, pine forest and logging roads - a genuinely different landscape for long-range and low flying.
hazards: Private forestry land, logging operations, 4WD and MTB traffic, sand kills motors
note: Outside the CTR and 8.9 km from Parakai, so airspace is clean - but you need the forestry manager's permission, not just a council park rule.

name: Waikowhai Park
access: Waikowhai Rd, Hillsborough. 20 min from CBD. Walk down to the wharf.
best: Bush, cliffs, a long wooden wharf and harbour water - the closest thing to a west-coast feel on the Manukau side.
hazards: Steep tracks, swimmers off the wharf, tide, dense bush behind
note: No permit. The wharf is the shot; the bush blocks LOS if you drop below the ridge. Pin is on the park itself; the old pin was 600 m north up a residential street.

name: Lynfield Cove
access: The Avenue, Lynfield, then the cove track.
best: Tiny sheltered cove with a bush backdrop and hardly anyone there - quiet water lines.
hazards: Mud at low tide, single-track access, no facilities
note: No permit. Pairs well with Waikowhai in one trip. The old pin was 1.8 km inland off Stranolar Drive. Pin is the reserve at the head of the cove, at the end of Lynbrooke Avenue.

name: Ceramco Park
access: Ceramco Park, off Great North Rd, Glendene.
best: Big flat fields and a stream — tuning and practice, not scenery.
hazards: Rugby and league fixtures, dog walkers, stream at the boundary.
note: West Auckland's equivalent of Lloyd Elsmore — a field, not a destination.

name: Wattle Bay
access: Wattle Bay Rd, Laingholm; park at the reserve at the end.
best: Tiny bush-ringed cove on the Manukau — sheltered, green water, almost nobody.
hazards: Steep bush tracks, mud at low tide, no phone coverage.
note: One of the few Waitakere-side bays you can legally fly — it sits outside the ranges park.
